selected_complete_public_types.name: completeKloosterman_weil
selected_complete_public_types.complete_source_header:
theorem completeKloosterman_weil (q : ℕ) [NeZero q] (a d : ℤ) :
    ‖completeKloosterman q (a : ZMod q) d‖ ≤
      (q.divisors.card : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (q.gcd (a.natAbs.gcd d.natAbs)) *
        Real.sqrt q

selected_complete_public_types.name: reciprocalInterval_fouvry
selected_complete_public_types.complete_source_header:
theorem reciprocalInterval_fouvry {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) (_ : NeZero q) (d : ℤ) (X Y : ℝ),
      X ≤ Y → Y - X ≤ q →
      ‖reciprocalInterval q d X Y‖ ≤
        C * Real.sqrt (q.gcd d.natAbs) * (q : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 + ε : ℝ)

selected_complete_public_types.name: reciprocalProgression_fouvry
selected_complete_public_types.complete_source_header:
theorem reciprocalProgression_fouvry {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ) (_ : NeZero q) (d b : ℤ) (v : ℕ) (X Y : ℤ),
      v.Coprime q → X ≤ Y →
      ‖reciprocalProgression q d b v X Y‖ ≤
        C * (1 + ((Y : ℝ) - X) / q) * Real.sqrt (q.gcd d.natAbs) *
          (q : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 + ε : ℝ)

selected_complete_public_types.name: iv3CorrelationProgression_fouvry
selected_complete_public_types.complete_source_header:
theorem iv3CorrelationProgression_fouvry {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (D d₁ n n₂ n₂' r s s' : ℕ) (a h h' : ℤ) (b v X Y : ℕ),
        0 < n → 0 < r → 0 < s → 0 < s' →
        (D * n₂ * n₂').Coprime (n * r * s * s') →
        v.Coprime (n * r * s * s') → X ≤ Y →
        ‖iv3CorrelationProgression D d₁ n n₂ n₂' r s s' a h h' b v X Y‖ ≤
          C * (1 + ((Y : ℝ) - X) / (n * r * s * s' : ℕ)) *
            Real.sqrt ((n * r * s * s').gcd
              (iv3CorrelationNumerator d₁ n n₂ n₂' s s' a h h').natAbs) *
            (n * r * s * s' : ℕ) ^ (1 / 2 + ε : ℝ)

next_shortest_concrete_lemma.name: Exact root-phase residue freezing and bounded packet Cauchy on original carriers
next_shortest_concrete_lemma.reason: After DifferenceReciprocity, the next obstacle to using any scalar spectral theorem is that the root phase and coefficient restrictions still depend on denominator variables. A generic smooth spectral result does not accept arbitrary jointly b,c,h-dependent coefficients. Freeze residue coordinates while retaining original coefficient products; this proves a usable separation rather than adding a hSpectral premise.
next_shortest_concrete_lemma.full_mathematical_statement: For fixed positive A and delta, any finite original positive n,v,w carriers and complex coefficient T(n,v,w,h), define packet(r,s,t) by n=r,v=s,w=t modulo A. The total signed sum equals the sum over (r,s,t) in (ZMod A)^3 of the same carrier-restricted packet. On each packet, stdAddChar_A((-a*h)*inverse(n*delta*v*w)) equals stdAddChar_A((-a*h)*inverse(r*delta*s*t)); it is a unit scalar depending on h and fixed packet labels, not on the remaining b,c indices. Hence ||sum_packets S||^2 <= A^3 sum_packets ||S||^2. The same statement remains valid for A=1; positivity/coprimality needed by the actual root-phase bridge must be discharged from its existing licenses.
next_shortest_concrete_lemma.elementary_proof: Partition finite carriers by their three residue maps. Congruent products are equal in ZMod A; apply congrArg inverse and stdAddChar. Apply finite complex Cauchy to all A^3 labels. Independent coordinate restriction multiplies the original coefficient functions by indicators; do not remove a coupled restriction until after a positive square.
